evaluation.AC01_fresh_identity: OBSERVED: one fresh 96 DPI capture with HWND/PID/title/rect/DPI, bound PrintWindow pixels, 49/49 display agreement and independent image digest agreement.
evaluation.AC02_regions_located: OBSERVED: the three mixed-script names and the Latin/Japanese label set were located in UIA and mapped to image coordinates; surrounding context-bar fields, the rail row, the inspector Goal label and the Dock candidates were measured too.
evaluation.AC03_text_versus_pixels: Each measured region has both a UIA string and bright ink inside its own rectangle, so presence in the accessibility tree alone is not being called rendering. Which ink band belongs to which substring is NOT_MEASURED without OCR; the observed band order is consistent with the UIA text order.

AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.missing_glyphs_tofu: OBSERVED on the retained crops (context-title.png, task-rail-item.png, inspector-goal.png): the Japanese strings are drawn as recognisable glyphs; no hollow missing-glyph box was seen. Limit: visual inspection of three crops at 96 DPI, not glyph-coverage or OCR proof.
AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.clipping: OBSERVED: every measured ink bbox keeps an interior margin on the half-open rectangles — the context title keeps 3 rows above and 3 below its rows 43–62; the rail item keeps 13 above and 13 below its rows 403–508; the wrapped inspector label keeps 12 above and 11 below its rows 389–438. No ink reaches a rectangle edge. Each inset is emitted by measure_text.py, not copied by hand.
AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.line_bands: OBSERVED: the rail row separates into four ink bands (12, 10, 14 and 10 rows tall) with starts 22, 21 and 27 px apart; the Japanese-sized band is 14 rows tall against 10–12 for the Latin bands. The taller band and the wider gaps are geometry, not an attributed cause: element padding, per-style line heights and fallback metrics are not separated here.
AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.baseline: OBSERVED within the context title: the Latin sample's ink bottom is row 58 and the Japanese sample's is row 59 — a one-row ink-bottom difference with the same 46–59 band. Neither run is clipped and the lines do not overlap. A per-run baseline metric from the shaping layer is NOT_MEASURED, and face resolution is not inferred from appearance.
AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.wrapping: OBSERVED on inspector-goal.png: the Goal label wraps '新製品キビジュ' / 'アル' inside the button, leaving a two-character second line. The full value is present in UIA and no ellipsis or truncation appears, so this is recorded as OBSERVED_NOT_DIAGNOSED, not as a demonstrated contract violation.
AC04_glyphs_clipping_lines_baseline.dock_line_separation: NOT_MEASURED for the Candidate Dock cards: the two text rows merge into one band under the four-empty-row rule, so per-line geometry there was not separated.
